title: Contract probes and runtime sensors for streaming & tool-call compatibility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add lightweight runtime sensors and contract probes that assert and record semantic compatibility across streaming, function/tool calling, and structured-output behaviors when API flags or versions change. The goal is to detect regressions early in canary and CI, provide actionable signal for rollbacks, and produce data for migration guides and automated compatibility reports.
acceptance_criteria: A set of probes can run in CI and on dedicated staging canaries that exercise: streaming partial-chunk boundaries, mid-stream tool-call interrupts, and structured-output schema evolution scenarios
Probe results are surfaced in Console with per-route and per-model regression metrics (error rate, schema mismatches, L0-L3 severity tags)
Automated alerts fire if probe baseline deviation exceeds thresholds and link to suggested rollback or mitigation playbooks
Probes include synthetic workloads and a harness for replaying recorded production traces with anonymized inputs
Documentation and a one-click enable/disable flag exist for running probes in dedicated/hosted/private deployments
tasks: Design probe contracts for streaming chunk semantics and define success/failure criteria
Implement lightweight runtime sensor library that can be injected into serving runtime (C++/Rust shim + Go admin hooks)
Build CI job templates that run probes against PR deploys and canary clusters
Expose probe metrics and traces in Console; add a dedicated 'compatibility' dashboard
Create migration checklist and sample curl/SDK commands for customers to validate their prompts against new flag changes
Write playbook for automated rollback decisions based on probe signals
testing_plan: Unit tests for probe library covering edge cases (partial tokens, truncated KV cache, tool-call abort paths)
Integration tests against runtime-1.22 build in staging with simulated latency and batch sizes
Replay of 48 hours of anonymized production traces against candidate releases and compare probe results to baseline
Introduce fault-injection tests (drop chunks, reorder packets, introduce schema changes) to validate probe sensitivity
Run probes as part of nightly canary and surface weekly regression summary to PM/EMs
decisions: Sensors will record both binary pass/fail and graded severity (info/warn/error) to allow threshold tuning
Probe harness will prefer trace replay over synthetic generation for higher signal-to-noise ratio
Initial probe coverage will focus on: streaming partial-emit semantics, tool-call handshake/state transitions, and structured-output schema compatibility
Probe library will be opt-in by default in Private deployments and enabled for Hosted by default in canary lanes only
